patient_identity.statement: F1 VI:1 matches the pedigree and clinical table: male33years, congenital onset.

genotype.statement: Homozygous NAV3 c.6325C>T,p.Gln2109Ter;hg38chr12:78197280C>T matches packet; source usesNM_001024383.2 and Fig2NP_001019554.1.

segregation.statement: Variant segregates with affected family1 individuals; VI:1,VI:2,VI:3 are TT and their motherV:2 is CT. Other branch parentsV:6,V:7areCT; VI:7isCT.
limitations: The assigned trio fatherV:1 has no displayed genotype; not all affected/unaffected pedigree members are tested. Sanger supplemental pair belongs to a differentF1branch.

phase.statement: Single homozygous variant supports recessive inheritance; no pair of different variants requires cis/trans assignment.
limitations: Biparental origin of both copies in the assignedF1siblings is inferred; their father lacks a displayed genotype. No independent phasing/UPD analysis performed.

causal_confidence.statement: Additional consanguineous families and segregating rare predicted-truncating alleles support NAV3-associatedNDD; paper classifies this nonsense allele pathogenic.
limitations: No patientRNA/protein or functional assay of these exact alleles in this paper. Truncation/NMD and loss of function are predicted; expression data are external reference tissue, not variant-specific validation. Table2ACMGcode lists are not independently re-scored; family1duplicatesPM2. Family2HSPG2co-occurrence complicates phenotype attribution and does not prove a modifier mechanism.

limitations: F1speech absent in main but first words/sentences present inTableS1. F3aggression/hyperactivity positive in main but negative inTableS1; some F3facial/excluded items not established.
